title: Vodafone Idea Ltd - 532822 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Vodafone Idea posted its first positive net subscriber addition since merger in Q1 FY27, with revenue up 6.0% YoY to Rs 11,689 Crore and Cash EBITDA up 13.5% to Rs 2,475 Crore.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 showed continued improvement: revenue rose 6.0% YoY to Rs 11,689 Crore, EBITDA reached Rs 5,034 Crore (43.1% margin), and Customer ARPU rose 10.2% YoY to Rs 195. Management reported the first positive net subscriber addition since the merger, led by postpaid and M2M, and a 24 bps YoY churn reduction. Capex was muted at Rs 1,930 Crore due to geopolitical supply-chain constraints, but orders of about Rs 9,000-9,100 Crore have been placed to be deployed over the next two quarters or less. Funding improved with Rs 1,183 Crore of warrant proceeds from the Aditya Birla Group, a first tranche of Rs 6,400 Crore in total, and rating upgrades to Crisil A-/Stable and ICRA A-(Stable).

segments.name: Consumer mobile (postpaid, prepaid)
segments.commentary: Postpaid net adds positive for 6-8 quarters per management; prepaid described as still needing work, with churn and gross-add quality improving. Total data usage rose about 28% YoY to 88.4 PB/day.

segments.name: M2M / IoT
segments.commentary: Net additions reportedly doubled over the last year; a dominant position in connected car IoT was cited. Management gave no subscriber breakup, but said M2M was a major driver of Q1 net adds.

segments.name: Enterprise (Vi Business)
segments.commentary: Demand was strong across connectivity, cloud, IoT, cybersecurity and other areas. No financials were disclosed for the segment.

guidance_outlook: Three-year targets unchanged: Cash EBITDA of 3x the FY26 level (FY26 was Rs 9,200 Crore), a revenue CAGR of about 16.8%, sustained net adds and double-digit revenue growth.
Capex of Rs 45,000 Crore over the next three years maintained; orders of Rs 9,000-9,100 Crore to be deployed over the next two quarters or less.
Roughly 3,500 4G sites per month on average going forward; 4G rollout to finish in about 18 months.
3-year network guidance: about 55,000-57,000 4G sites and 86,000-90,000 5G sites; 5G may run into a third year because of fibre needs.
Organic ARPU expected to keep growing from the Rs 195 blended base, a little better than current trend.
Over 200 more cities to be covered with 5G over the next two quarters; 5G currently live in over 200 cities and over 16,000 sites.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex of Rs 1,930 Crore, muted by geopolitical supply-chain constraints.
Orders of about Rs 9,000-9,100 Crore placed with Ericsson, Nokia, Samsung and other partners; supplies have started.
Added nearly 3,000 unique broadband towers in the quarter and over 15,600 sites in the last twelve months; 4G population coverage at 87.0%.
5G live in over 200 cities across all 17 circles where Vi holds 5G spectrum; over 16,000 5G sites now.
Funding architecture: SBI-led PSU bank consortium (6-7 banks), Indian private banks, and ECB with foreign banks; first tranche Rs 6,400 Crore raised. PSU bank talks still open.
demand_pricing: Customer ARPU Rs 195 (+10.2% YoY, +2.6% QoQ), up for 20 consecutive quarters; management says it is the highest growth in the industry.
ARPU drivers: 2G to 4G upgrades worth about Rs 230-240 ARPU uplift; NonStop Hero versus unlimited data about Rs 20-35 uplift; about 3-4% of customers upgraded each quarter.
66% of customers on 4G/5G smartphones and 34% on 2G, per management.
Retail network of 2,600-plus stores across 650-plus towns.
Management said there was no dip in postpaid despite Airtel's Fast Lane/priority plan, and that the Q1 seasonal urban-to-rural migration is a timing effect.

qa_highlights.question: Net debt position, and M2M subscriber split?
qa_highlights.answer: Bank debt is Rs 211 Crore (down about Rs 500 Crore in the quarter), plus Rs 3,300 Crore of NCDs raised in December 2025, for total debt of Rs 3,489 Crore versus Rs 4,001 Crore in Q4. Management did not give an M2M subscriber breakup.

qa_highlights.question: Is the M2M growth masking a postpaid ex-M2M decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denied any postpaid decline, saying postpaid net adds have been positive for 6-8 quarters. It attributed the gap to timing in bootstrap businesses and said there are no prepaid M2M subscribers.

qa_highlights.question: Funding: how much of the Rs 5,200 Crore balance is debt versus non-fund based, and from whom?
qa_highlights.answer: The balance comes from ECB and Indian private banks as a mix of funded debt and non-fund based facilities; the split was not disclosed. Management said the Rs 9,100 Crore order book also draws on the opening cash balance.

qa_highlights.question: Network opex flat for several quarters despite site rollout; how will it trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said internal efficiencies have offset rollout costs for two quarters. Diesel inflation may show up in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Sharp rise in roaming access charges?
qa_highlights.answer: This came from higher wholesale roaming participation, which is cash-accretive but carries a lower percentage margin. Management said it is not structural and not linked to intra-circle roaming.

qa_highlights.question: Tower or infrastructure sharing with BSNL?
qa_highlights.answer: Vi already has tower sharing with BSNL. No other tower sharing is in discussion.

risks_watch: Capex execution: Rs 9,100 Crore of orders must be deployed within about two quarters, against Rs 1,930 Crore in Q1, which was constrained by geopolitical supply issues.
Prepaid subscriber trend and the Q1 VLR decline management attributed to seasonality; July traction to be verified.
Pending PSU bank (SBI-led) debt closing, and the debt/non-fund split of the Rs 5,200 Crore incremental funding.
Competitive risk from Airtel's Fast Lane/priority plan in postpaid.
Network opex pressure from diesel inflation and rising roaming costs.
Quality of the exceptional gain: Rs 1,816 Crore from remeasurement of earmarked CLAM shares recurs each quarter and is non-operating.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operating momentum and guidance, with the CEO repeating that all 7 critical parameters are trending positively. Cautious and somewhat evasive on the postpaid ex-M2M question, the M2M subscriber split, and the funding breakdown, which management declined to quantify.
key_quotes: We delivered our first quarter of positive net subscriber additions since merger and we will continue this momentum.
The Customer ARPU has now been increasing for 20 consecutive quarters.
We intend to deploy all of this capex over the next 2 quarters or less.
The defining theme for this quarter is momentum.

growth.why: Management held the three-year plan (revenue CAGR ~16.8%, Cash EBITDA 3x FY26 by FY29) and backed it with Rs 9,000-9,100 Cr of placed orders with Ericsson, Nokia and Samsung plus a 3,500 sites/month rollout, but Q1 capex of Rs 1,930 Cr was well below the Rs 45,000 Cr three-year plan run-rate due to supply constraints, and no utilisation figure was given.
